title: Fixed Point Exploration For CV-QKD IR QC-MET-LDPC Toward Hardware Implementation
authors: Guilherme Vergne de Oliveira, Mauro Queiroz Nooblath Neto, Micael Andrade Dias, Francisco Revson Fernandes Pereira, Francisco Marcos de Assis, Valéria Loureiro da Silva, Nelson Alves Ferreira
abstract: High-speed LDPC decoding is a major bottleneck in CV-QKD and motivates hardware acceleration with fixed-point arithmetic. This work compares SPA, MSA, and NMS under a unified low-SNR fixed-point framework using common graph, matrix, and quantization settings. Multiple formats are evaluated through FER, and average iterations. The results show that performance depends strongly on the interaction between decoder rule and numerical precision. SPA achieved the best overall performance. For reduced-complexity decoders, Q16.8 was the lowest consistent precision, with NMS outperforming MSA. Practically, SPA with Q8.4 offered the best balance between reliability and hardware efficiency for large-scale implementations.
summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck in CV-QKD by comparing three iterative decoding algorithms—SPA, MSA, and NMS—under strict fixed-point arithmetic constraints. By simulating performance across various precisions at low SNR, the authors determined that SPA provides the most reliable results, recommending a specific Q8.4 format for practical hardware deployment.
main_problem: High-speed LDPC decoding is a major bottleneck for practical Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution (CV-QKD), requiring efficient hardware acceleration.
main_result: The Sum-Product Algorithm (SPA) demonstrated the best overall performance, while SPA using Q8.4 precision offered the optimal balance between reliability and hardware efficiency for large-scale implementation.
method: A comparative analysis was performed on three message-passing decoding algorithms (SPA, MSA, NMS) within a unified fixed-point arithmetic framework.
model_or_system: The study models the error correction process using LDPC codes applied to CV-QKD reconciliation at very low Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNR). The core mathematical tool is the quantization of real values into fixed-point representations.
key_observables: Frame Error Rate (FER) and average number of decoding iterations ($ ar{I}$).
important_parameters: Fixed-point precision (e.g., Q8.4, Q16.8), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR $\le 0$ dB).
main_assumptions: The fixed-point model abstracts constraints expected in future hardware realization, such as those on FPGAs.
figures_summary: Figures compare FER vs. SNR curves for different decoders and precisions, illustrating SPA's superior robustness across varying numerical formats.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the necessity of LDPC codes for CV-QKD hardware acceleration, details the unified fixed-point decoding framework, and concludes with a comparative evaluation of SPA, MSA, and NMS performance metrics.
why_interesting: While focused on classical coding theory applied to quantum communication, the explicit analysis of numerical precision limitations (fixed-point arithmetic) is highly relevant for designing resource-constrained quantum hardware accelerators.
